judge_reasoning: The opponent is not required to spend three Ballista counters killing Spell Queller. They can take the 2 combat damage and retain all four counters. After Shock resolves, Ballista remains a 4/4 with 2 damage marked. When Felidar Guardian blinks Saheeli and Saheeli activates −2, she immediately falls from 3 loyalty to 1. The opponent can then remove one counter from Ballista, which remains alive as a 3/3 with 2 damage marked, and deal 1 damage to Saheeli. Saheeli dies before the copied Guardian can blink her, ending the loop. Thus the proposed line does not win against a reasonable defensive response.
model_solution:
1. Play **Island**, giving you five available mana. Activate **Saheeli Rai’s +1**, dealing 1 damage to your opponent and putting Saheeli at 6 loyalty.

2. Attack with **only Spell Queller**. Keep Reckless Fireweaver and Whirler Virtuoso out of combat.

3. Under the note’s stipulated damage-minimizing Ballista play once combat begins, your opponent must spend at least **three counters killing Spell Queller**. Neither opposing creature can block it, so shooting it down reduces combat damage from 2 to 0. Walking Ballista now has at most one counter.
   
   Keeping Fireweaver out of combat is important: it cannot be killed by that final Ballista shot.

4. In your second main phase, if Walking Ballista is still alive, cast **Shock** targeting it. Its remaining counter cannot save it: either Shock kills it, or removing its last counter puts it into the graveyard. Its one remaining shot cannot kill Fireweaver or Saheeli.

5. Cast **Felidar Guardian**, using the remaining four mana. If Ballista already died, simply leave the unnecessary mana unused. Use Guardian’s enters-the-battlefield ability to blink **Saheeli Rai**. She returns as a new permanent with 3 loyalty and can activate a loyalty ability again this turn.

6. Activate Saheeli’s **−2**, copying Felidar Guardian. The token is an artifact, so **Reckless Fireweaver deals 1 damage** to your opponent. Use the token Guardian’s ability to blink Saheeli, returning her with 3 loyalty again.

7. Repeat step 6 until Fireweaver has dealt lethal damage. With your opponent at 9 life, nine artifact Guardian tokens suffice. This wins in the second main phase; no further attack is necessary.

Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions

This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones

Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.
